textContent.text: "I'll take it," I said, holding out my plate. Usually, Bernie loved Pops's homemade pizza, and we always fought over any leftovers. But tonight, Bernie didn't even look up from his plate when Pops offered up the last piece. Weird.

After a quick glance at Bernie, Pops plopped the pizza onto my plate. I dug into the last slice of deliciousness and looked back and forth between Pops and Bernie. What was the deal? They were both being strangely quiet tonight. Pops busied himself cleaning crumbs from the table, and Bernie still gazed at his plate, absentmindedly pushing around the remnants of his pizza crust.
Breaking the awkward silence, I babbled between bites of pizza, "Hey, Bernie, I heard you talking to someone on the phone earlier. Did the coffee shop finally call you back?"
Bernie grimaced and mumbled something unintelligible.
"Huh? I thought that might've been them since it's been almost a week since your interview. You'd think they'd get back to you by—"
Pops cleared his throat loudly, cutting me off. "Ellie, why don't you come help me with the dishes?" He quickly hopped up from his chair and motioned me towards the kitchen.
"But I'm not even finished with my pizza yet," I muttered with my mouth full.
Pops gave a meaningful look toward Bernie, who was staring at his plate, then looked back at me and nodded his head pointedly at the kitchen.

textContent.text: "How's the surf report looking?" Nana came into the sunroom with her coffee, her eyes shining with eagerness.

"It's a bit choppy…" Vivian said, then remembered to repeat it again more loudly. She was not used to the changes in her grandmother. These days, Nana's hearing was not as sharp as it once was, and her night vision was so poor she couldn't drive after dark.
"I'm stoked for those waves!" Nana crowed. "Should we head out soon?"

Nana's spunky attitude hadn't changed, despite the physical effects of aging. And a year ago, when Vivian had wanted to give up on learning to surf, Nana had told her they would figure it out together. Vivian had been shocked. Surfing at Nana's age? Was that safe? But Nana had reminded her that when she was younger, she'd played softball and rugby, and she had never shied away from trying something just because it might be difficult.
